newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Former Jamaica PM breaks silence on illness.
newsitem.headline: Former Jamaica PM breaks silence on illness.

text.p: Former Jamaican Prime Minister Michael Manley broke his silence on his health on Wednesday, saying he was confined to bed and had "good days and not-so-good days."
Manley, 72, has not been seen in public for nearly six months and no details have been given on the state of his health or the nature and extent of his illness.

In a brief statement released on Wednesday through his public relations agency, Manley said: "Since the article I wrote on battling cancer last year, I have had some good days and some not-so-good days."
He added, "Although confined to bed recently I continue to manage and supervise my various personal and public affairs."
Manley expressed gratitude for messages of support he had received.

The former leader was diagnosed with prostate cancer in 1990 and a bout with pneumonia on an official visit to Washington robbed him of one-third of his lung capacity. He stepped down in 1992, citing poor health.

There was no official word on his condition until Dec. 18, when Prime Minister P.J. Patterson issued a statement wishing him a speedy recovery on behalf of the heads of government of the 14-member Caribbean Community.
Manley's family said last month the former prime minister was "very, very ill" but has not commented further.
